title: Learning sentiment from word sequences
question: How much of a sentiment model's behaviour comes from its embeddings, recurrent architecture and regularisation?
mechanism: Movie-review classification compared learned and pretrained embeddings, LSTM variants, dropout and attention.
contribution: Shared implementation guidance and substantive report review; individual sentence authorship in mixed notes is not independently resolved.
outcome: Experiments were reviewed, but these exports do not establish a final numerical improvement.
discuss: How much of a sentiment model's behaviour comes from its embeddings, recurrent architecture and regularisation?

title: What actually improves an image classifier?
question: Which gains survive a properly trained baseline and controlled architectural comparisons?
mechanism: CIFAR experiments compared VGG pooling, normalisation and dropout choices, followed by residual-network comparisons.
contribution: Baseline and architecture guidance, with review distinguishing replication from original invention.
outcome: Student notes report improved accuracy, but the runs were not reproduced in this recovery. Architectural novelty is not established.
discuss: Which gains survive a properly trained baseline and controlled architectural comparisons?

title: Attention is not the only useful change
question: When attention helps, is it doing more for the task than a simpler regularisation change?
mechanism: Sentiment models combined dynamic-length inputs, embeddings, bidirectional recurrence, pooling, dropout and attention visualisation.
contribution: Training/data-pipeline guidance and detailed technical review are retained in the shared project record.
outcome: Attention reportedly exceeded the baseline but underperformed dropout. Combining all promising changes remained a recommendation, not a verified result.
discuss: When attention helps, is it doing more for the task than a simpler regularisation change?

title: Choosing what the network learns next
question: Should a classifier learn from easy examples, difficult examples, or a curriculum that changes with the model?
mechanism: Curriculum, anti-curriculum and dynamic sampling were compared with random sampling in VGG-based image classification.
contribution: Shared design notes cover example difficulty, data providers, comparison structure and repeated-run statistics.
outcome: Training and small gains are reported, but a sufficiently specified statistical comparison is absent. Not every proposed extension was completed.
discuss: Should a classifier learn from easy examples, difficult examples, or a curriculum that changes with the model?

title: A drawing is both an image and a sequence
question: What can a model learn from the order of the strokes that it misses in the finished image?
mechanism: QuickDraw classification combined CNN image features with bidirectional-LSTM stroke features, feature fusion and three supervised heads.
contribution: The shared notes document my tutorial support, design guidance and technical discussions. The execution logs document the students' work.
outcome: The logs report a multitask benefit and document reruns after validation/test augmentation problems. No final aggregate metric was independently audited.
discuss: What can a model learn from the order of the strokes that it misses in the finished image?

title: Making a small visual dataset useful
question: How do we separate useful transfer and augmentation from an improvement that only reflects a weak baseline?
mechanism: Low-data image classification was explored through augmentation, regularisation and transfer-learning choices.
contribution: Interim technical review reframed the problem and requested explicit architectures and evaluation. Official allocation supports the tutoring relationship.
outcome: The precise application and dataset are unresolved; no final performance result is established.
discuss: How do we separate useful transfer and augmentation from an improvement that only reflects a weak baseline?

title: When the baseline will not reproduce
question: What can we conclude about a proposed change before we can reproduce the model it is meant to improve?
mechanism: DenseNet experiments investigated minority-class behaviour and imbalance; the exact application and mentioned attack method remain unresolved.
contribution: Technical review required baseline reproduction, per-class metrics and reproducible configurations.
outcome: Interim results underperformed the reference baseline. The linked results spreadsheet was not reread in this pass.
discuss: What can we conclude about a proposed change before we can reproduce the model it is meant to improve?

title: Recognising individuals in an imbalanced dataset
question: How do we evaluate individual recognition when a few classes dominate the examples we have?
mechanism: Whale-tail identification raised fine-grained recognition, class imbalance, transfer learning and overfitting questions.
contribution: Review focused on transfer-versus-scratch ambiguity, held-out evaluation and the compute risk of proposed architecture tuning.
outcome: Interim experiments suggested overfitting; no defensible final held-out result was recovered. RL-based architecture tuning remained a proposal.
discuss: How do we evaluate individual recognition when a few classes dominate the examples we have?

title: Does a defence survive a different attack?
question: Are we learning a robust model, or a defence that works against the attacks we happened to test?
mechanism: Adversarial-robustness work examined whether defences generalise across different attacks.
contribution: Interim and final technical reviews examined reproducibility, the evaluation questions and limitations.
outcome: Completed experiments are described in the review, but exact attack implementations and numerical results are absent from the exports. Universal robustness is not established.
discuss: Are we learning a robust model, or a defence that works against the attacks we happened to test?

title: What has a sign-recognition model learned?
question: What does reconstructing an input tell us about the representation used to recognise it?
mechanism: Sign recognition compared convolutional architectures and regularisation, with decoder-based reconstruction used to inspect fixed representations.
contribution: Technical reviews challenged weak baselines, ambiguous data splits and overly strong interpretations of reconstruction experiments.
outcome: Experimental and interpretability work was reviewed. Video translation and real-time classification were future directions, not completed systems.
discuss: What does reconstructing an input tell us about the representation used to recognise it?

title: Curiosity as a learning signal
question: When does seeking unfamiliar states improve the policy, and how should we measure that separately from exploration itself?
mechanism: Reinforcement-learning experiments compared PPO with random-network-distillation exploration and later investigated world models.
contribution: Repeated project discussions and reviews addressed metric reporting and the justification for changes in research direction.
outcome: Experiments were reported without a clear comparative reward table in the export. The world-model addition is not established as Antreas's original suggestion.
discuss: When does seeking unfamiliar states improve the policy, and how should we measure that separately from exploration itself?

title: Learning how to reason from few examples
question: Can a learner adapt to a new reasoning task, rather than merely recognise examples from familiar classes?
mechanism: The project explored MAML-based few-shot relational reasoning and the construction of custom tasks and datasets.
contribution: Technical review clarified meta-learning versus few-shot learning, the MAML procedure and valid benchmark comparisons.
outcome: Interim work is documented; a final result is absent. Results from a different task setting cannot be treated as directly comparable.
discuss: Can a learner adapt to a new reasoning task, rather than merely recognise examples from familiar classes?

title: Evaluating the evaluator through face outpainting
question: How do we know whether an image-generation metric is measuring the quality we actually care about?
mechanism: GAN evaluation was examined using face outpainting as a concrete generative task.
contribution: A sent technical review reframed the research around whether the evaluation measures are useful, rather than merely whether a model can generate faces.
outcome: Review contribution only. Exact metric names, numerical outcomes and group allocation are not established.
discuss: How do we know whether an image-generation metric is measuring the quality we actually care about?

title: World models on a smaller compute budget
question: Which parts of a world-model pipeline still earn their cost when the compute budget becomes much smaller?
mechanism: A scaled-down World Models study used CarRacing to investigate model-based reinforcement learning under limited compute.
contribution: A sent review establishes substantive technical and manuscript feedback, separate from the other curiosity-driven RL project.
outcome: Experiments were discussed, but exact scores were not independently recovered. This is review work, not ownership of the model or training runs.
discuss: Which parts of a world-model pipeline still earn their cost when the compute budget becomes much smaller?

title: Where does a captioning model get its gains?
question: If a caption improves, how do we establish whether the encoder, decoder or training setup made the difference?
mechanism: CNN–RNN image captioning explored encoder, decoder and attention choices, with later architectural alternatives considered.
contribution: Technical review focused on research framing, reproducible experiments, model selection and unsupported encoder-versus-decoder conclusions.
outcome: Experiments were reviewed without an independently verified final performance claim. Transformer and relational alternatives remained suggestions.
discuss: If a caption improves, how do we establish whether the encoder, decoder or training setup made the difference?

title: When an audio classifier will not fit
question: Before changing the model, can we establish why the existing audio classifier is not fitting its training data?
mechanism: Instrument classification on IRMAS brought together audio preprocessing, aggregation and training diagnostics.
contribution: Technical review examined splits and repeated runs, and treated non-fitting training curves as possible optimisation, gradient or implementation problems.
outcome: Baseline difficulties were documented. A diagnostic hypothesis is not a verified repair or performance improvement.
discuss: Before changing the model, can we establish why the existing audio classifier is not fitting its training data?

title: Translating maps across visual domains
question: Can an image translator change a map's style while retaining the relationships that make it a map?
mechanism: Relational CycleGAN research explored modern-to-antique map translation, with follow-on research development.
contribution: Contemporary correspondence corroborates the team relationship and an invitation to continue towards a paper. Specific code ownership is not isolated.
outcome: A report and continued collaboration are documented; recovered planning notes do not establish a final gain or publication.
discuss: Can an image translator change a map's style while retaining the relationships that make it a map?

title: A smaller model still needs the right test
question: What does an efficiency comparison mean if the benchmark and metric do not match the task we claim to solve?
mechanism: An efficiency project evolved from distillation planning towards quantisation, heatmaps and bounding-box conversion in the reviewed report.
contribution: Technical review challenged benchmark justification, annotation methods, task–metric mismatch and single-seed evaluation.
outcome: The report was revised, but a compression benefit remains unverified.
discuss: What does an efficiency comparison mean if the benchmark and metric do not match the task we claim to solve?

title: Captioning: reproduction before novelty
question: What have we learned by changing the dataset, and what would justify claiming a new method?
mechanism: Image-captioning work investigated recurrent alternatives and possible interpretability studies.
contribution: Technical review clarified the baseline and task, and separated replication from an original methodological contribution.
outcome: Reviewed experiments largely replicated existing methods on another dataset. Proposed attacks and autoencoder extensions were not completed work.
discuss: What have we learned by changing the dataset, and what would justify claiming a new method?

title: Learning the style of an ink-wash painting
question: When a translation model fails, is the problem the objective, the data, or the implementation?
mechanism: Photo-to-ink-wash CycleGAN work combined dataset collection, qualitative inspection and classifier-based evaluation.
contribution: Technical review distinguished the GAN objective from the application, sharpened the research questions and explored possible implementation problems.
outcome: Unsuccessful methods were documented. The record does not establish that the suspected problems were repaired or that translation ultimately succeeded.
discuss: When a translation model fails, is the problem the objective, the data, or the implementation?

title: What a few-shot improvement actually tells us
question: Does better performance on a few-shot task establish the broader claim we want to make about generalisation?
mechanism: MAML++-based few-shot work investigated character recognition and claims about bias and generalisation.
contribution: Technical review corrected inner-/outer-loop data assumptions and challenged the inference from task improvement to reduced data bias.
outcome: The report described task-specific improvements, but these do not establish a general bias-reduction result.
discuss: Does better performance on a few-shot task establish the broader claim we want to make about generalisation?

title: Emotion, language and the evaluation pipeline
question: How much of the apparent improvement comes from the model, and how much from how we built and split the data?
mechanism: The project developed emotion classification and explored emotion-conditioned reply generation, with dataset construction central to the comparison.
contribution: Technical review examined oversampling, validation splits, model selection and fixed-budget comparison claims.
outcome: Experiments were reported, but parts of the task remained ambiguous in the review. No general superiority claim is established.
discuss: How much of the apparent improvement comes from the model, and how much from how we built and split the data?

title: Translating musical style
question: Which aspects of a piece should change when we translate its style, and which should remain recognisably the same?
mechanism: Symbolic-music style transfer combined CycleGAN-style translation with sequence modelling.
contribution: Tutor evidence and technical review support task formalisation, motivation and calibration of research claims.
outcome: A final report is catalogued, but the preliminary review supplies no verified performance or publication result.
discuss: Which aspects of a piece should change when we translate its style, and which should remain recognisably the same?

title: Which representations transfer to a new world?
question: Does a representation help a policy transfer, or merely fit the world on which we trained it?
mechanism: DARLA-style representation learning and beta-VAE ideas were investigated on CoinRun with DQN/PPO control.
contribution: Tutoring and technical review supported benchmark feasibility, reproducing a baseline before extending it, and compute-aware research scope.
outcome: Training and reproduction were still in progress in the notes. Evolutionary and meta-learning extensions were proposed, then deprioritised; final gains are not established here.
discuss: Does a representation help a policy transfer, or merely fit the world on which we trained it?

title: Learning interactions between sparse features
question: Which feature interactions are worth learning explicitly when most of the input is sparse and categorical?
mechanism: Click-through prediction explored field-weighted factorisation models, compression and attention-style feature interactions on Criteo data.
contribution: Technical review addressed the task, architecture and experimental configurations. Individual authorship of every design choice is not established.
outcome: A report is catalogued; performance gains were not independently verified. The literature list is not an inventory of personally trained models.
discuss: Which feature interactions are worth learning explicitly when most of the input is sparse and categorical?

title: Bringing pretrained vision into style translation
question: Where should a pretrained representation enter a generative system, and which parts should we allow to change?
mechanism: Monet-style CycleGAN work considered how to integrate CLIP image representations into a translation pipeline.
contribution: A joint technical call records code walkthroughs, generator/discriminator integration advice, frozen-versus-tuned comparisons and staged ablations.
outcome: The assistance is documented, but the team's own planning document and final outcomes are missing. It is a separate project from the text-to-face work.
discuss: Where should a pretrained representation enter a generative system, and which parts should we allow to change?

title: Making a normalising flow smaller
question: How much of a generative model can we remove before the efficiency gain stops being worth the modelling loss?
mechanism: Normalising-flow compression explored pruning, product quantisation and low-rank approaches to efficient generative modelling.
contribution: Tutoring and technical review supported problem motivation, task definition and experiment design.
outcome: Planning, review and the existence of a final report are established. Compression gains and personal implementation are not verified.
discuss: How much of a generative model can we remove before the efficiency gain stops being worth the modelling loss?

title: Recovering detail in astronomical images
question: How do we tell restored astronomical structure from plausible detail invented by the model?
mechanism: Astronomical image restoration explored denoising and frame enhancement, with CycleGAN and DnCNN comparisons in the recovered report catalogue.
contribution: Technical review addressed degradation and task definitions, low-resolution prototyping, dataset construction and quantitative alongside qualitative evaluation.
outcome: Data preparation and a selected frame-enhancement direction are documented. The final comparison was not reread in this pass and no numerical gain is claimed.
discuss: How do we tell restored astronomical structure from plausible detail invented by the model?

title: Finding the bottleneck in an audio pipeline
question: Is the slow part the architecture, the data pipeline, or a mismatch in how we are using the pretrained model?
mechanism: Rainforest-audio work connected spectrogram classification, pretrained-model adaptation, CNN efficiency and data-loading diagnostics.
contribution: Two help calls record architecture inspection, timing advice, HDF5 loading discussion, dependency debugging and a live PyTorch tensor-shape/head-dimension demonstration.
outcome: Demonstration execution appears in the transcript but was not independently rerun. The student's training remained problematic; no final improvement is verified. Formal reassignment to Antreas is not confirmed.
discuss: Is the slow part the architecture, the data pipeline, or a mismatch in how we are using the pretrained model?

title: Learning a sequential decision policy
question: How do we tell whether a decision policy generalises rather than exploiting the period on which we tuned it?
mechanism: RL trading research considered fitted-Q and double-DQN methods, recurrent attention and alternative reward definitions.
contribution: Tutor evidence supports research guidance; shared technical planning is not proof of personal trading-system implementation.
outcome: The notes warn that plans may differ from the final project. Some adaptations were reported and reproduction requested. No live-trading or profit claim is established.
discuss: How do we tell whether a decision policy generalises rather than exploiting the period on which we tuned it?
